screenshots.details: Current final hub art + DOM menu

captures.title: Bathroom hub — final art
captures.whatToNotice: The default hub boot: the washing machine is the cycle selector, with the final bathroom plate and DOM menu. Anatomy is selected and both cycle cards are readable at 1280×720.
captures.alt: Bathroom hub with the washing machine and two cycle cards

captures.title: Hub settings — text scale and reduced motion
captures.whatToNotice: Settings are part of the hub, not a separate screen. Text size is shown at 125% and reduced motion is On; both apply to the hub and the next cycle.
captures.alt: Bathroom hub with the settings panel open at 125% text scale

captures.title: Hub — Silicon cycle selected
captures.whatToNotice: Selecting the Silicon cartridge changes the machine display and the selected card. The same start button and player modes apply.
captures.alt: Bathroom hub with the Silicon cycle card selected

captures.title: Bathroom hub — placeholder art
captures.whatToNotice: The procedural placeholder path remains available for comparison. The layout and controls are the same, but the final scene plate and sprites are replaced by generated shapes.
captures.alt: Bathroom hub rendered with procedural placeholder art

captures.title: Launch — washing-machine spin
captures.whatToNotice: The launch cinematic spins the drum before the shrink. The hub panel is hidden, but the skip control stays available for accessibility.
captures.alt: Washing-machine drum spinning during the launch cinematic

captures.title: Launch — shrink and arrival
captures.whatToNotice: The tiny astronaut appears at the machine exit after the shrink flash. This is the hand-off from the bathroom frame to the pack fiction.
captures.alt: Tiny astronaut arriving at the washing-machine exit after the shrink

captures.title: 03 Nerve Forest — co-op wide shot
captures.whatToNotice: Two players start at the entry checkpoint with the Node Run beats and full HUD visible. The final sky is the only wired background layer in this slice. The dendrite branches, soma, hillock and myelin-node catwalk are floating platforms, so the whole puzzle is played above the ground.
captures.alt: Two players at the Nerve Forest entry checkpoint with the final sky

captures.title: 03 Nerve Forest — key art (no HUD)
captures.whatToNotice: A clean view of the final Nerve Forest scene with the HUD and feedback layers hidden. Use it as a page or thumbnail background.
captures.alt: Nerve Forest scene with the HUD hidden

captures.title: 03 — Neuron Keeper dialogue
captures.whatToNotice: The Neuron Keeper introduces the threshold rule in a speech bubble anchored to the character. The dialogue is DOM, so it scales with text size and stays readable.
captures.alt: Neuron Keeper dialogue bubble in Nerve Forest

captures.title: 03 — scan feedback
captures.whatToNotice: Scanning the one-way pathway returns a concept cue in the world. The cue names the concept before the player opens the log.
captures.alt: Scan cue for the one-way pathway in Nerve Forest

captures.title: 03 — concept log
captures.whatToNotice: The concept log shows discovered terms, definitions and relationships. Undiscovered concepts stay listed as hidden so the player can see the shape of the syllabus.
captures.alt: Concept log overlay with the discovered sensory and motor pathways entry

captures.title: 03 — system map
captures.whatToNotice: The map exposes the current node and revealed connections. It is a navigation aid, not a minimap; unknown paths stay unlabeled.
captures.alt: System map overlay showing the Nerve Forest node

captures.title: 03 — threshold gate
captures.whatToNotice: The threshold gate is the Node Run progression marker on the soma platform. It opens after the stimulus counter reaches two inputs; the platform route, not gate collision, is what forces the player to climb.
captures.alt: Threshold gate and dendrite pads in Nerve Forest

captures.title: 03 — one dendrite input ready
captures.whatToNotice: One input is below threshold: the first dendrite pad is active, but the threshold gate is still closed. The counter and beat tracker make that state visible.
captures.alt: First dendrite input active while the threshold gate remains closed

captures.title: 03 — threshold reached
captures.whatToNotice: Two inputs reach threshold and the threshold gate opens. The spike is all-or-none from here; the terminal is the next required step.
captures.alt: Both dendrite inputs active and the threshold gate open

captures.title: 03 — exit gate open
captures.whatToNotice: The terminal relay opens the exit gate. The player can now leave Node Run and the debrief becomes available.
captures.alt: Exit gate open after the terminal relay in Nerve Forest

captures.title: 03 — debrief prompt
captures.whatToNotice: The debrief asks the player to explain the threshold rule in their own words. The evidence panel starts in the missing state until the answer is recorded.
captures.alt: Nerve Forest debrief overlay with an empty answer

captures.title: 03 — debrief answer recorded
captures.whatToNotice: Recording the answer updates the evidence panel and enables Finish level. The answer stays visible so the player can review it before continuing.
captures.alt: Nerve Forest debrief with a recorded answer and evidence

captures.title: 04 Muscle Effector — co-op wide shot
captures.whatToNotice: The ferry starts inactive. The presynaptic tower, elevated cleft bridge and postsynaptic receptor platform are all off the ground; the motor terminal, ACh packet, receptors and muscle gate are visible in final sprite art.
captures.alt: Muscle Effector room with the Endplate Ferry objects

captures.title: 04 Muscle Effector — key art (no HUD)
captures.whatToNotice: A clean Muscle Effector layout with the UI hidden. Sprite art is final; the muscle background layer is not wired yet, so the plate is a gradient.
captures.alt: Muscle Effector scene with the HUD hidden

captures.title: 04 — Endplate Ferry active
captures.whatToNotice: Starting the motor terminal activates the ferry beats. The HUD now tracks the Ca²⁺ window, ACh carry and receptor binding.
captures.alt: Endplate Ferry active with the motor terminal and ferry beats

captures.title: 04 — P2 carrying the ACh packet
captures.whatToNotice: P2 carries the ACh packet; the HUD marks the carrier and the prop gets a carried outline. In co-op, only P2 can carry.
captures.alt: P2 carrying the ACh packet in Muscle Effector

captures.title: 04 — nicotinic receptor interaction
captures.whatToNotice: The carrier prompt changes to Place ACh packet at the nicotinic receptor. The matching triangle receptor is the target; the circle receptor is the decoy.
captures.alt: P2 carrying ACh at the nicotinic receptor

captures.title: 04 — pulse and muscle wave
captures.whatToNotice: P1 pulses the motor terminal after ACh binds. The screen caption confirms the signal and the muscle gate carries the wave effect.
captures.alt: Motor terminal pulse and muscle response in Muscle Effector

captures.title: 04 — debrief prompt
captures.whatToNotice: The Muscle Effector debrief asks for the Ca²⁺ → ACh → receptor → response chain. The evidence panel is still missing the written answer.
captures.alt: Muscle Effector debrief overlay with an empty answer

captures.title: 04 — level complete
captures.whatToNotice: Finishing the debrief opens the completion overlay, with evidence export, replay and return-to-hub actions.
captures.alt: Signal restored completion overlay after Muscle Effector

captures.title: Silicon — Interrupt Loop wide shot
captures.whatToNotice: The Silicon fixture uses the same two-player shell and HUD on the circuit-board plate. The sensor console, rising interrupt-line platforms, route plug and controller/CPU catwalk form the puzzle spine above the ground.
captures.alt: Interrupt Loop room on the Silicon circuit board

captures.title: Silicon — key art (no HUD)
captures.whatToNotice: A clean circuit-board view with the UI hidden. The sky is lossless WebP; the circuit atlas is still a placeholder SVG.
captures.alt: Silicon circuit-board scene with the HUD hidden

captures.title: Silicon — CPU Core dialogue
captures.whatToNotice: The CPU Core explains that it is the output side, not the integration point. The dialogue choice checks the same distinction as the transfer gate.
captures.alt: CPU Core dialogue bubble in the Interrupt Loop

captures.title: Silicon — interrupt puzzle state
captures.whatToNotice: The sensor is latched and P2 is carrying the route plug. The controller socket is the integration point; the CPU socket is the decoy.
captures.alt: Interrupt puzzle with the sensor latched and P2 carrying the route plug

captures.title: Silicon — concept gate overlay
captures.whatToNotice: The transfer console opens the concept gate. This is the only wired concept-gate overlay in the current slice; 03's authored gate is not loaded.
captures.alt: Concept gate overlay opened from the Silicon transfer console

captures.title: 03 Nerve Forest — solo
captures.whatToNotice: Solo mode keeps P2 inactive and gives P1 both pulse and carry. The same scene and HUD remain, with the co-op tether disabled.
captures.alt: Solo Nerve Forest with P1 at the Neuron Keeper

captures.title: Accessibility — 125% text scale
captures.whatToNotice: The pause settings show 125% text scale active. The UI font scale applies to the HUD, overlays and dialogue without changing the world.
captures.alt: Pause settings with 125% text scale selected

captures.title: Accessibility — reduced motion
captures.whatToNotice: Reduced motion keeps the feedback text and captions and removes the decorative transitions. The active setting is visible in the page state, even in a still.
captures.alt: Nerve Forest feedback caption with reduced motion enabled
